transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess what finally pushed me to come in is that my eating has just been... all over the place lately. Um, some weeks I barely even touch dinner, I just don't have the appetite for it. And then other nights, I find myself just standing in the kitchen, eating crackers and sweets long after everyone else has gone to bed. It's just really inconsistent and I don't know why.
After these nights where you find yourself eating a lot, do you ever try to compensate by making yourself sick, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?

No, I don't do any of that. I mean, I might feel a bit guilty about it the next day, but I've never tried to make myself sick or taken laxatives or anything like that. And I definitely don't exercise to try and make up for it. I just... I just eat the food and that's the end of it.
When you find yourself eating a lot, especially late at night, do you feel like you can't stop yourself or that you're not in control of how much you're eating?

No, I wouldn't say I feel out of control. It's not like a compulsion or anything where I can't stop. I just... I'm awake, I'm restless, and I just keep eating. But I could stop if I really wanted to, I just don't in the moment.
Do these changes in your eating habits cause you a lot of distress or interfere with your daily life?

Well, the eating itself isn't the biggest problem, but things have definitely been harder lately. I've fallen behind on my facilitator training, and... well, I do some work on a private blog, and I just can't keep up with it right now. My projects and the way I try to explain things have just gotten really hard to organize. Plus, there's been a lot of tension at home, which makes it tough to keep any kind of normal routine with my husband. So, yeah, it is interfering with my life.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, lately?

Yeah, I have been. I go through these stretches where... well, the whole house just feels gray and heavy. I'll sit at the kitchen table just feeling completely empty, even though nothing terrible has actually happened that day. It just sort of settles over me.
Have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy, like your blog work or anything else, lately?

Yeah, I have. Things I used to really look forward to... they just feel like chores now. Like, I usually love going to my book club, or cooking, visiting art galleries, even just tending to the rose beds in the yard. But lately, I just keep putting them off. I don't really have the drive to do any of it.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to think clearly, concentrate, or make decisions lately?

No, not really. I mean, I haven't noticed any major changes with that. Like I said, organizing my blog has been tough, but I wouldn't say I'm having trouble thinking clearly or making decisions overall. Just... lack of motivation, I guess.
Have you noticed a big drop in your energy lately, or do you often feel tired even when you haven't done much?

No, not really. I don't feel physically tired or wiped out. It's... well, like I was saying, it's more just that I don't have the motivation to start anything. But my actual energy levels seem pretty normal, even when I haven't done much all day.
Have you noticed a significant decrease in your appetite or lost weight recently, even when you weren't trying to diet?

Well, actually, that's kind of what finally pushed me to come in. My eating has just been all over the place lately. Um, some weeks I barely touch dinner, I just don't want it. But then other nights, I'll just stand in the kitchen eating crackers and sweets after everyone else has gone to bed. So, yeah, my appetite is definitely off.
How long have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day like this?
Well, those periods where I just feel gray and guilty, and I lose interest in everything... if I add it all up, it's been about seven months total.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or felt like your thoughts are slowed down?

No, not really. I don't think I'm moving or talking any slower than I usually do. Um, and my thoughts seem to be going at their normal pace, too. Nobody has pointed anything out to me about being slow, anyway.
Have there been days when you've had absolutely no interest or pleasure in anything at all, not even the things you usually enjoy?

Yes, definitely. Things I used to look forward to, like going to my book club, trying out new recipes, or even just visiting art galleries... they just feel like chores now. Even tending to my rose beds, which I used to love, is something I just keep putting off. I just don't have any interest in doing them anymore.
Have you experienced any significant weight loss recently, or do you feel excessively guilty or worthless, even when there's no clear reason for it?

Well, my weight hasn't really changed much. But the guilt... yes. It gets pretty bad sometimes. I can spend hours just replaying really small things in my head. Like, if I buy an expensive tube of paint pigment, or if I just snap at my husband over something silly. I'll just dwell on it and start feeling like I've completely ruined the whole household because of it. It feels really heavy, even though I know it doesn't make total sense.
Have you ever felt like life wasn't worth living, or had thoughts about harming yourself when you've been feeling down?

Sometimes, yes. Um, on the worst nights, I do catch myself thinking that it would just be easier if I didn't wake up the next morning. But I haven't actually made any kind of plan to hurt myself or anything like that. It's more just a thought I have when I'm feeling really low.
Have you had days where you feel like nothing, not even the things you used to love, brings you any pleasure at all—like everything just feels flat or meaningless?

Yes, I think that's what I was trying to say earlier. It's exactly like that. The things I usually look forward to—like my book club, cooking, the art galleries, and tending my rose beds—they really just feel like chores now. Everything just goes flat, and I just keep putting them off because that feeling of enjoyment just isn't there.
